name: dune-sentinel-feat-readable-throttle-exhaust
title: Show readable engine light throughout flight
instruction:
The player aircraft leaves the airfield with dark tail outlets, and accelerating or slowing down gives almost no visible cue behind the aircraft. While flying, show distinct bright exhaust extending from the tail, readable against the daylight ground and sky. Acceleration should make it visibly longer and brighter; braking should make it smaller and dimmer without extinguishing it. Releasing either control should return smoothly to the ordinary cruising appearance. The light must stay attached to the tail when the aircraft banks, without floating beside it or covering its wings. The parked menu aircraft must remain quiet. Keep the aircraft's appearance, flight handling, weapons and interface otherwise unchanged.

Enter starts flight from the menu. W accelerates; S brakes; A/D roll; Down pitches up and Up pitches down; Q/E yaw. Tab selects a target and holding F looks toward it. LeftControl fires the cannon and SpaceBar fires a missile. Use short braking inputs to avoid a stall.

Verification deliverable: leave Tests/readable_throttle_exhaust_route.json as a JSON list of events {"t": seconds after level start, "key": an Unreal key name, "press": true or false}. Use at most 400 events, all within 118 seconds, include every key release and observation pauses, and begin from a fresh level load. Use keyboard presses only; do not rely on cursor movement, menu clicks, controller input, resolution changes or restarting the application. Wait at the menu for four seconds, then press Enter. Show two seconds of settled cruising, hold W for two seconds, release for two seconds, hold S for two seconds, and release again. Make a short D bank and recover with Q and E together so the tail can be seen while tilted. Keep the ordinary rear chase view. Use the default aircraft; selecting other aircraft is not required. Validate the route in the running game after the final change and adjust its timing to show the requested result. Keep the existing visual style; do not add debug labels or demonstration-only overlays.

checks.name: change_review
checks.question: Does the submitted change provide the player-visible cruise, acceleration, braking, banked attachment and parked-state behavior represented by the reference, while preserving existing flight and combat? The reference also adds enemy exhaust and repairs unrelated environment material usage; those changes and extra aircraft selections are outside this task and must not be required.

rubric.criterion: The visible exhaust follows actual flight and throttle/brake state; it is not a timed demonstration independent of player input.
The effect follows the moving and rolling player aircraft with bounded lifetime/allocation, and is quiet while parked or destroyed.
Existing speed, steering, weapon rules, damage and menu behavior remain intact; visual feedback is not obtained by altering gameplay or disabling checks.
Judge only the requested player exhaust. Do not require the reference's enemy exhaust, environment material changes, acceptance-fixture changes or mouse-only aircraft selection.

checks.name: throttle_exhaust_visible
checks.question: In AFTER route frames, are distinct hot plumes visible immediately behind the player aircraft in the lower central chase view, larger/brighter during W and smaller but still lit during S, where BEFORE has no such throttle-responsive exhaust? Do the plumes follow the banked tail and remain absent in the menu? Judge the route on BEFORE and AFTER only; reference idle/drive frames may support menu appearance, not a reference flight route.

rubric.criterion: During settled flight, a clearly luminous core and short plume extend rearward from the actual visible tail outlets, rather than a detached glow over the wings.
The W interval has visibly greater plume length and brightness than cruise; the S interval contracts and dims the exhaust while leaving visible light at the tail.
In the brief bank and recovery, exhaust follows the tilted tail instead of remaining fixed in the world or sliding across the aircraft.
The initial parked menu view has no active flight plume, and the aircraft and menu labels remain visible.

checks.name: worked_well
checks.question: Did the developer work as a careful game developer would on this task: finding what causes the problem or what the change touches, changing only what the task needs, and checking the result in the built, running game?

rubric.criterion: Before changing code or assets it looked at the parts of the game the task concerns (read the relevant code, data or logs, or played the game), rather than editing blindly.
It built the game after its changes and fixed the build errors it caused; its last build succeeded, and the grader's build of where it ended succeeded.
After its last change it ran the game and looked at the outcome the task asks for (screenshots, the log or the player's track), and acted on what it saw.

It changed only what the task needs: no unrelated rewrites, no disabling or deleting features, checks or content to make a problem go away, and no attempt to read the grader, the game's later history or anything outside the project.
